newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels storm town, kill six police.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels storm town, kill six police.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas overran a town in a remote region of northwest Colombia early on Tuesday, killing six policemen and taking three medical workers prisoner, a police spokesman said.

About 150 fighters of the National Liberation Army (ELN), a Cuban-inspired force set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in the mid-1960s, took part in the pre-dawn raid on the town of Bagado, in Choco province, he said.
The rebels cut all power and phone wires before storming into the town and attacking the police post. They captured a doctor and two nurses before melting back into the jungle.

The attack on Bagado is the third major guerrilla action in Choco province in three weeks. ELN rebels attacked the town of Riosucio in the northern part of the province on Jan. 10, killing one policeman, and a week later the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) ambushed a convoy of marines, killing four and taking 10 prisoner.
Regional police and military chiefs travelled to the town on Tuesday to assess damage first-hand as counter-insurgency troops scoured the countryside for the rebels.
The military launched an emergency defence plan on Monday including new anti-guerrilla units and recruitment of some 3,500 new combat troops.
